claims.text: Severe lattice distortion is responsible for the dynamic mechanical behavior of single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Multiple principal elements induce severe lattice distortion in the HEA.
Lattice distortion creates a complex local energy landscape.
The complex local energy landscape hinders dislocation glide during rapid deformation.
Hindered dislocation glide enhances dynamic yield strength.
Hindered dislocation glide increases strain-rate sensitivity under dynamic loading.
At high strain rates, the HEA will have a higher dynamic yield strength than the conventional solid-solution alloy baseline.
At high strain rates, the HEA will have greater strain-rate sensitivity than the conventional solid-solution alloy baseline.
A conventional alloy with fewer principal elements has less lattice distortion than the HEA.
The comparison should use single-phase alloys with similar grain size and homogenized microstructure.
Both alloys should be tested in compression at room temperature using identical specimen geometries and controlled high strain rates.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to homogenized, single-phase HEAs under room-temperature dynamic loading.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to multiphase HEAs or to HEAs whose microstructures have been substantially altered by additional thermal processing.
The magnitudes of the yield-strength increase and strain-rate sensitivity depend on composition, lattice-distortion magnitude, and microstructural details.
Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in either dynamic yield strength or strain-rate sensitivity relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to find microstructural evidence of lattice-distortion-induced impediment of dislocation motion would falsify the hypothesis.
